close_reason:
Expanded the existing two-pass-update-loop rationale comment block (src/mailbox.rs:661-698) with an explicit 'Defense notes (bd:JMAP-q2wa.13)' subsection enumerating the four arguments against future single-pass or topological-sort 'simplifications', verbatim from the bead text:

1. serde_json::Map iteration order is not a documented semver contract.
2. Two-pass mirrors RFC 8620 §5.3 creates-before-updates ordering.
3. Topological sort is a net negative abstraction here.
4. Role-swap proof obvious in two passes, complex in one.

Comment-only change; no behaviour change. The bd:JMAP-q2wa.13 inline citation makes the defense discoverable from git-blame so a future contributor running 'why are there two passes?' through history lands on this bead's body. Quality gates: fmt + clippy --all-features --tests + mailbox tests pass.
description:
src/mailbox.rs:676-702 — handle_mailbox_set partitions the update map into a vacating pass (role: null patches) and a non-vacating pass, then runs them in two separate for-loops with roles_successfully_vacated tracking the intermediate state.

A future contributor might suggest collapsing into a single pass on the grounds that 'HashMap iteration is deterministic in Rust 1.65+' or 'a topological sort would do this more cleanly'. Defend the current shape:

- HashMap iteration order in serde_json::Map is currently insertion order (BTreeMap-like) but this is NOT guaranteed across serde_json versions. Relying on it for atomicity is a bug latent under a dep bump.
- The two-pass model directly mirrors the RFC 8620 §5.3 'creates run before updates' ordering rule, applied within the update phase. The structure communicates intent at a glance.
- A topological sort would require building a dependency graph (which role is freed for whom) — net negative abstraction vs. two short for-loops.
- The 'role-swap in a single request' case (A vacates inbox, B claims inbox) is one of the easier-to-reason-about correctness properties of Mailbox/set, and the two-pass shape makes the proof obvious. Combining would require a complex argument about ordering within a single pass.

The inline comments at 676-697 document the invariants and the why. Preserve them if a refactor is attempted.
title: Defend: Mailbox/set two-pass update loop for atomic role swap
